heading: Rotate = Transpose + Reverse
body:
90° clockwise rotation is TWO simple moves:

**1. Transpose** (flip along diagonal)
**2. Reverse each row**

No extra space needed. Both steps modify in-place.

heading: Why j starts at i
body:
During transpose, `for j in range(i, n)` swaps each pair **once**.

If you started at 0, you'd swap `(i,j)` with `(j,i)` then later swap them back — undoing the transpose!

label: Crux · Python

q: What is the time complexity of this solution?
explain: Two nested loops (transpose + reverse) both visit all n² elements.
